1.explanation:
• src/config-provider/index.jsx – Contains the implementation of ConfigProvider, its internal cache (Map/table) and the componentWillUnmount hook that tries to remove entries. This is where the leak originates under SSR.  
• config-provider/index.md & index.en-us.md – Show the public API, usage patterns and describe how context and cache are set up. Useful to understand how users consume and configure the provider.  
• config-provider/demo/basic.md – A minimal usage example to reproduce mounting/unmounting behavior.  
• config-provider/demo/components.md – Demonstrates how ConfigProvider wraps child components, which helps simulate nested providers and cache key generation.  
• config-provider/demo/consumer.md – Illustrates how consumers access cached configuration and confirms that unmount should clear cache entries.  
Together, these files allow you to reproduce the SSR mount/unmount cycle, inspect and modify the cache behavior, and implement a manual cleanup API if needed.
1.bug_scenario: When running a React SSR service under load, we observe that each request (or each page render) mounts a new ConfigProvider instance, but because React’s componentWillUnmount is never called during SSR, the internal cache never gets cleaned. In the memory‐profile snapshot provided, you can see a Map object whose internal “table” array holds dozens of stale ConfigProvider instances that should have been GC’d. The UI in the screenshot shows total heap size growing (193.98 MB shallow, 150.08 MB retained), and when drilling into the retainers, a Map → table → multiple ConfigProvider entries is displayed, proving the leak.
